h: Dyspnea and chest pain 3 weeks after hip replacement, clear chest film: diagnosis?
p: Recent orthopedic surgery is a major DVT/PE risk even with prophylaxis; the chest film is often normal. Next steps are CT pulmonary angiography then anticoagulation.

h: Pancreatic cancer with migratory thrombophlebitis: tender cord on medial leg, which vessel?
p: Trousseau syndrome: recurrent migratory superficial thrombophlebitis as a paraneoplastic hypercoagulable state, classic for pancreatic cancer. The great saphenous is the superficial vein running medial to the femoral condyle.

h: Alcoholic given glucose, then confusion and nystagmus: deficient vitamin?
p: Wernicke encephalopathy: confusion, ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus, ataxia. Give thiamine before glucose in at-risk patients.

h: Painless bleeding at 13 weeks, grape-like vesicles, hyperemesis: usual karyotype?
p: Complete mole is diploid (46,XX), all paternal DNA, with no fetal parts and high hCG. Partial mole is triploid (e.g., 69,XXY).

h: High homocysteine with normal methylmalonic acid: deficient vitamin?
p: Folate deficiency raises homocysteine only; B12 deficiency raises both homocysteine and methylmalonic acid. Homocysteine is a thrombosis risk factor.

h: Surgical neck of humerus fracture: muscle supplied by the injured nerve?
p: The axillary nerve (C5-C6) supplies deltoid and teres minor, and gives sensation over the lateral shoulder. Supraspinatus is suprascapular nerve; subscapularis is the subscapular nerves.

h: Best substance to estimate renal plasma flow?
p: PAH is filtered and almost completely secreted, so its clearance approximates renal plasma flow. Inulin clearance measures GFR.

h: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus becomes sensitive after drug-free generations: mechanism?
p: Resistance genes (e.g., vanA) often sit on plasmids; without selective pressure the plasmid can be lost and the bacteria revert to sensitivity.

h: Itchy grouped vesicles on elbows and knees: associated condition?
p: Dermatitis herpetiformis is the skin manifestation of celiac disease (IgA deposits in dermal papillae), treated with a gluten-free diet and dapsone.

h: Toddler with head injury, shifting story, parents refuse a private interview: diagnosis?
p: Inconsistent history, delay or evasiveness, and refusal to let the child be interviewed alone are red flags. Physicians are mandated reporters.

h: Fatty meal triggers gallbladder contraction: which hormone?
p: CCK (from I cells) contracts the gallbladder, relaxes the sphincter of Oddi and stimulates pancreatic enzymes, causing biliary colic after meals when gallstones are present.

h: Diabetic with an eye turned down and out: accompanying sign?
p: CN III palsy: eye down and out, ptosis, and mydriasis (spared in ischemic diabetic cases). Facial droop is CN VII; smell is CN I.

h: Pancytopenia with blasts holding needle-shaped (Auer rod) inclusions: leukemia?
p: Auer rods (myeloperoxidase-positive) mark myeloblasts of AML. APL (t(15;17)) is treated with all-trans retinoic acid.

h: Contralateral weakness with lost vibration, tongue deviates toward lesion: syndrome?
p: Anterior spinal artery occlusion: corticospinal (contralateral hemiparesis), medial lemniscus (lost vibration and proprioception) and CN XII (tongue deviates toward the lesion).

h: Sigmoid colon atresia: which fetal vessel was disrupted?
p: Intestinal atresias arise from in-utero vascular accidents; the hindgut (distal transverse to upper rectum) is supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery.

h: Psychosis in a patient worried about weight gain: best antipsychotic?
p: Ziprasidone and aripiprazole are the most weight-neutral antipsychotics. Clozapine and olanzapine cause the most weight gain; ziprasidone needs QT monitoring.

h: Pulsatile abdominal mass, hypotension, back pain in a smoker: diagnosis?
p: Smoking, age, male sex and hypertension are the main AAA risks. Rupture is a surgical emergency; unstable patients go straight to the operating room.

h: Joint infection 6 days after arthroplasty, nafcillin-resistant gram-positive cocci: organism?
p: S. aureus is the leading cause of early postoperative joint infection; nafcillin resistance means MRSA, treated with vancomycin.

h: Hematuria, deafness, family history of kidney failure: defect?
p: Alport syndrome (X-linked in most): COL4A5 defect causes hematuria, sensorineural hearing loss and eye problems (anterior lenticonus).

h: Primary CNS lymphoma in AIDS: associated virus?
p: AIDS-related primary CNS lymphoma is EBV-driven, presenting as a ring-enhancing lesion. Toxoplasmosis is the main mimic; JC virus causes PML.

x: keyed chelator disputable (encephalopathy would favor dimercaprol/EDTA)

h: Pancreas divisum: what embryologic step failed?
a: Fusion of ventral and dorsal pancreatic buds
p: Normally the ventral bud rotates and fuses with the dorsal bud; failure of fusion leaves separate ducts (pancreas divisum), which can cause pancreatitis.

h: Organophosphate poisoning after atropine, persistent muscle spasms: next drug?
p: Atropine treats muscarinic effects only; pralidoxime reactivates acetylcholinesterase at the nicotinic synapse (before aging). Physostigmine and carbachol would worsen cholinergic excess.
